disclosures.name: TestWeakCertCache
disclosures.signature: timed out waiting for expected ref count
disclosures.reason: TestWeakCertCache exercises the certificate cache built on weak.Make and runtime.AddCleanup. The test drops both certificates (`certA = nil`, then `certB = nil`, each followed by runtime.GC()) and polls four seconds for the cache's cleanup to delete the entry; on windows it times out at the SECOND poll, since the first is trivially true while certB lives. weak.Make, runtime.AddCleanup and runtime.GC() are correct: a converted probe of the same cache (11 arms, every one passing in Go) clears the weak pointer and runs the cleanup inside the same runtime.GC() call whenever the last strong reference lived in a frame that has returned, including after the object survived an earlier GC, under TieredCompilation on and off and with JIT inlining off. It fails only in the test's own shape: `certA, err := wcc.newCert(...)` is a two-result call, and on windows/amd64 its 16-byte (ж<Certificate>, error) ValueTuple returns through a hidden stack buffer that the JIT never clears. In JitDisasm FullOpts both calls pass that buffer (rcx=[rsp+0xC8], [rsp+0xA8]) and copy the results out to registers, and the gword slots sit in the prolog's zero-init block, untracked, so the CLR reports them live to the method's end and the certificate stays reachable until TestWeakCertCache returns. The one-result twin passes with inlining off, which isolates the tuple return as the axis. Linux's SysV ABI returns the pair in RAX:RDX, and the test passes on linux (0.31 s), hence windows only; darwin is added only if a run there fails it. Same class as sync's TestOnceXGC and TestPoolGC.

A converted probe of the same cache at f8fe15c97e (11 arms, every one passing in Go 1.26.10) clears the weak pointer and runs the cleanup inside the same runtime.GC() call whenever the last strong reference lived in a frame that has returned, including after the object survived an earlier GC, under TieredCompilation on and off and with JIT inlining off. disclosures.name: TestBogoSuite
disclosures.reason: The test delegates to BoringSSL's own test runner, spawned as `go test .` in the boringssl module -- a child that carries Go's default 10-minute test-binary deadline, which neither the package's code nor the host controls (the test passes no -timeout, in either language). Inside that wall the runner spawns the shim once per case -- 5,481 spawns in this configuration -- and the shim IS the converted test host, a self-contained single-file executable whose process start (bundle open, CLR startup, JIT over the converted-stdlib closure) measures 2.61 s where Go's statically linked test binary starts in 0.038 s (the framework-dependent shape measures 3.30 s); the ~69x that remains is structural to the deployment shape. A ReadyToRun composite publish (+161 s, 181.5 MB) cuts shim startup to 0.74 s, and driven directly with the wall lifted the runner completes the whole configuration -- 3,242 cases, 861 PASS / 2,381 allow-unimplemented SKIP, zero failures, ok end to end -- in 1,316 s on a 6-core host and 1,046.3 s on a second machine, against the 600 s wall the test itself carries: 2.2x over on the 6-core host, down from ~20x without ReadyToRun. Later measurements show that what bounds the run is the host's start-up, not TLS throughput: one launch through the runner was measured at 0.8 to 1.2 s on 4-core hosts, against Go's 38 ms, and most of that is the converted host starting up -- package initialization across the converted standard library -- not the handshake. The 3,527 launches the runner makes at Go 1.26.10 therefore take well over the 600 s wall on such a host, while a host with more parallel capacity finishes them inside it, and there the converted side matches all 3,527 of Go's BoGo verdicts. The suite executes exactly the cases Go executes and skips exactly the ones Go skips, and the partition (861 runnable / 2,381 skipped) is contract-determined and load-invariant: it held across four runs on two machines under roughly 4x differing timeout pressure, with contention moving tests only inside the runnable set, so a different split would be a real change, not noise. The TLS interop capability itself is proven by value in the same suite: with `-bogo-filter Client-Verify-ECDSA-TLS1` the converted host completes a TLS handshake with certificate verification against BoringSSL as the peer, PASS in 14 s end to end including the module download and runner build. This entry fires only on a host whose launches miss the runner's own 600 s deadline. On a host where they finish, the root passes on both sides and the entry does not fire. It retires when the host's start-up brings the suite inside that deadline on the slowest host class validation runs on. A second, environmental arm: a host without the BoringSSL module never reaches the signature above (`bogo_shim_test.go:414`, the runner ran and outlived its deadline); it fails fifty lines earlier at `bogo_shim_test.go:364`, `failed to download boringssl`, and Go fails there too, identically -- with GOMODCACHE pointed at an empty directory and GOPROXY=off both runtimes report `--- FAIL: TestBogoSuite (0.61s)` off that one line. That arm is admitted only in the host-conditional fail/fail shape, where Go itself failed the same way; in the Go pass / C# fail shape the primary signature governs alone. It does not retire the entry: on a host that has the module but whose launches miss the runner's 600 s wall, the Go side fans out every BoGo row in under a minute while the converted side does not finish, so the pinned divergence is live there.
disclosures.history: The test delegates to BoringSSL's own test runner, spawned as `go test .` in the boringssl module — a child that carries Go's default 10-minute test-binary deadline, which neither the package's code nor the host controls (the test passes no -timeout, in either language). Inside that wall the runner spawns the shim once per case — 5,481 spawns in this configuration — and the shim IS the converted test host: since 2026-08-27 a self-contained single-file executable (the shape that retired the class's relocatable-executable entry), whose process start (bundle open, CLR startup, JIT over the converted-stdlib closure) measures 2.61 s where Go's statically linked test binary starts in 0.038 s -- the framework-dependent shape this entry was minted against measured 3.30 s, so the single-file publish bought ~0.7 s and the ~69x that remains is structural to the deployment shape. The ReadyToRun rung was measured 2026-08-28 (the empty-the-class commission): R2R composite publish (+161 s, 181.5 MB) cuts shim startup to 0.74 s, and driven DIRECTLY with the wall lifted the runner completes the whole configuration -- 3,242 cases, 861 PASS / 2,381 allow-unimplemented SKIP, ZERO failures, ok end to end -- in 1,316 s against the 600 s wall the test itself carries: 2.2x over on this 6-core host, down from ~20x. The wall is now THROUGHPUT-bound, not startup-bound: at the measured slot cost the zero-startup (AOT) floor computes to ~980 s here, so no startup work alone clears it on this host class -- the entry retires when managed steady-state TLS throughput on the sweep host crosses the runner's own deadline, and the interop itself is no longer in question at any width — it is what the artifact IS, not how far an implementation has got. Measured 2026-08-18: the runner reaches ~267 of 5,481 cases at its wall even with 16 parallel shim workers — a ~20x shortfall no deadline the test can express would close — then exits without writing its results JSON, which selects exactly the failure arm this signature pins. The TLS interop capability itself is not in question and is proven by value in the same suite: with `-bogo-filter Client-Verify-ECDSA-TLS1` the converted host completes a TLS handshake with certificate verification against BoringSSL as the peer, PASS in 14 s end to end including the module download and runner build. CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-29 on a second box (i9), and this is the first measurement whose numbers are produced by GO'S CONTRACT rather than partly by a harness defect: 861 PASS / 2,381 SKIP / 0 FAIL, exit 0 — identical to the record above on all three buckets — wall 1,046.3 s, about 20% faster than this box and still not crossing the 600 s deadline. What changed underneath it: the arc exposed two ordering defects in the converted test HOST, and before they were fixed 1,902 of these cases failed on a flag-parse ordering bug rather than on anything about TLS (the host ruled on an unrecognized flag before the package's TestMain could install the flag.Usage that exits 89, which BoGo reads as unimplemented-and-skip; and the host's own parse ran before TestMain at all). So the disclosed shape was partly an artifact of the harness, and is no longer: the suite now executes exactly the cases Go executes and skips exactly the ones Go skips. Same verdict, entirely different evidence. The partition is also now known to be contract-determined and load-INVARIANT — 861 runnable / 2,381 skipped held across four runs on two machines under roughly 4x differing timeout pressure, with contention moving tests only inside the runnable set and never across the skip boundary — so a future re-measure that reports a different split is reporting a real change, not noise. Retirement condition unchanged and sharper for it: this entry retires when managed steady-state TLS throughput on the sweep host crosses the runner's own 600 s deadline. Same self-retiring texture as os/exec's relocatable-single-file entries: publish the host with fast startup (ReadyToRun/AOT) and this row starts passing, the disclosed count stops matching, and the sweep fails until the entry is removed. SECOND ENVIRONMENTAL ARM (2026-08-28, the bogo skip-parity lane): the signature above is `bogo_shim_test.go:414` — the arm taken when the runner RAN and outlived its own deadline. A host that never had the BoringSSL module does not reach it; it dies fifty lines earlier at `bogo_shim_test.go:364`, `failed to download boringssl`, and GO DIES THERE TOO, identically, at the same line, for the same reason — measured by pointing GOMODCACHE at an empty directory with GOPROXY=off, where both runtimes report `--- FAIL: TestBogoSuite (0.61s)` off that one line. Until that arm was admitted (`hostConditionalSignature`) the comparison called the converted side MOVED and crypto/tls could not validate AT ALL on such a host: `TestBogoSuite: Go="fail" C#="fail" (failure does not match the disclosed host-limit signature "bogo failed: exit status 1")`. It is admitted ONLY in the host-conditional fail/fail shape, where Go itself failed the same way and the converted side is provably not the half that moved; in the Go pass / C# fail shape the primary signature still governs alone. NOTE this does NOT retire the entry, and the same lane measured why: the entry's retirement condition is the throughput one above, and on a capability-PRESENT host that misses the runner's 600 s wall — the i7-5820K, 2026-08-28, 400 matched + 2 disclosed against a banked 3643 + 1, its Go side fanning out all 3,242 BoGo rows in 50-66 s — the pinned Go pass / C# fail divergence is exactly as live as the day it was written. Retiring it there would convert a measured divergence into an undisclosed one. RE-WORDED 2026-11-08 (COORD ruling, PLAN-rebank-1-26-10-3.md section 5), at the go1.26.10.3 full-count bank. Three sentences of the visitor reason changed; their replaced text, verbatim: (1) `The wall is throughput-bound, not startup-bound: at the measured slot cost the zero-startup (AOT) floor computes to ~980 s on that host, so no startup work alone clears it on this host class.` -- replaced because docs/phase4/DATA-bogo-startup.md (P1, 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06, linux/amd64, 4 cores) measured the launch as start-up-bound: 1.18 s a launch through the runner, 0.17 s of it the handshake, about 0.9 s package init (the extension-method scan included), projecting about 1,085 s for 3,527 launches. (2) `This entry retires when managed steady-state TLS throughput on the sweep host crosses the runner's own 600 s deadline; like os/exec's relocatable-single-file entries it is self-retiring: once the converted side passes, the disclosed count stops matching and the sweep fails until the entry is removed.` -- replaced because, from 1.26.10.3, crypto/tls is banked at the full count where BoGo completes (COORD F2, 2026-11-07). The class G canary on G-LAPTOP (f58605e59a, 2026-11-07) completed it at 4920 matched + 1 disclosed, with this entry listed as orphaned and the comparison still validated, so the entry stays for hosts that miss the wall rather than self-retiring. (3) `It does not retire the entry: on a host that has the module, the Go side fans out all 3,242 BoGo rows in 50-66 s while the converted side misses the runner's 600 s wall, so the pinned divergence is live.` -- scoped to a host whose launches miss the wall. The registered block it pairs with is 3,527 (run-validated-sweep.ps1's table, moved to _roster.ps1 by the same branch). RANGED 2026-11-08 (COORD ruling): the first re-word stated P1's point reading in the present tense -- `one launch through the runner costs about 1.18 s on a 4-core host, of which the handshake itself is about 0.17 s and about 0.9 s is package initialization across the converted standard library. The 3,527 launches the runner makes at Go 1.26.10 therefore take about 1,085 s on that host class` -- and a later direct reading did not reproduce the figure, so the visitor text now states the range both readings fall in. The two source readings: (1) P1, docs/phase4/DATA-bogo-startup.md sections 3, 5 and 8 (2026-11-05/06), linux/amd64, a 4-core Xeon at 2.1 GHz, master 586cf44726 (and b0b48783dc for the probe breakdown), a shim wrapper timing each launch exec-to-exit: 1.18 s a launch through the runner, 0.17 s handshake, about 0.9 s package init; 1,950 launches in 601 s at the wall, projecting about 1,085 s for 3,527. (2) H, 2026-11-08, a 4-core i7 at master 72043c1a66, a direct reading: 0.77 s wall (equal to CPU) a launch, against Go's shim at about 38 ms a case. Neither reading came from the BoGo test's log record, which the converted testing package caps at 65,536 characters (testing/TestExecution.cs, MaxRecordCharacters) -- H's earlier 324-case figure, read from that record, was withdrawn for that reason.
disclosures.hostConditional: The GO side is decided by network reachability of the pinned boringssl module, which `go test` downloads and builds BoringSSL's own runner from, and by how far that runner gets inside the 10-minute deadline Go's test binary carries by default — so per host and per run the Go baseline passes, expands into its 3,243-row case matrix, or fails.

notes: On Apple silicon (osx-arm64) the converted package prefers the AES-GCM cipher suites, as Go does there. The converted standard library is built for amd64 and runs as a native arm64 process on Apple silicon, so it reads the processor's AES and PMULL support from internal/cpu's arm64 flags, which are filled as Go's darwin start-up fills them. Before they were filled, the package found no AES hardware on Apple silicon and preferred ChaCha20-Poly1305, where Go on the same machine prefers AES-GCM. On every other platform the preference is unchanged.
